representative_questions.question: How does the amount of absorbed CO2 affect the glass transition temperature (Tg) of PMMA?
representative_questions.expected_answer: The absorption of CO2 plasticizes the polymer and reduces the Tg; specifically, it decreases from 103 °C to -12.5 °C when 39.3% CO2 is incorporated, averaging a 3 °C reduction for every 1% increase in CO2 absorbed.

representative_questions.question: How does the relationship between saturation temperature (Tsat) and glass transition temperature (Tg) determine the physical state of the PMMA-CO2 mixture?
representative_questions.expected_answer: The system is in a rubbery state when the saturation temperature is greater than the glass transition temperature (Tsat > Tg), and it is in a glassy state when the saturation temperature is below the glass transition temperature (Tsat < Tg).

representative_questions.question: What method was used to determine the minimum foaming temperature of the PMMA-CO2 system?
representative_questions.expected_answer: Saturated samples were immersed in a silicone oil bath at foaming temperatures (Tf) ranging from -20 °C to 120 °C in 5 °C intervals; the minimum foaming temperature was identified as the average of the two adjacent temperatures where the sample transitioned from transparent (no foaming) to opaque (bubble formation).
